prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map depicts a flat outdoor basketball court with a smooth brightness gradient receding from the ground at the camera wearer's feet (about 1–1.5 m below the head-mounted camera) toward the distant background and night sky. In frames 1–3, as the wearer looks downward along the left boundary line, two backpacks rest on the ground in front of the wearer: a nearer bag at roughly 1.2–2 m (approaching closest in frame 2, just outside standing arm's reach unless the wearer bends down) and a second bag with a white shirt and water bottle about 1.5 m further ahead (2.5–3.5 m from the wearer), alongside sandals and a jump rope, while a person in shorts stands 6–8 m ahead in frame 1 and approaches to about 4–5 m in frame 3 with their upper body cropped at the top edge. As the camera pans right and tilts up in frames 4–5, a second person in a red shirt and blue pants appears on the court to the right at roughly 4–5 m in frame 4 and 3–4 m at the far left edge of frame 5 (partially cropped), with background light poles, trees, and a basketball hoop silhouette visible at 10–20 m in frame 4. Nothing is within immediate standing arm's reach (<1 m) of the camera wearer or the other people, though the person in frame 4 has their own hand raised to their face. Compared to the motion-blurred and darkly lit RGB frames, the depth map clearly isolates the 3D protrusions of the bags, straps, sandals, and background hoop against the ground plane, but it is unreliable on thin items like the jump rope in frame 3 (which disappears into the floor gradient) and on the person in frame 3 (whose blurred figure merges into the dark background).
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground regions on the court across the five frames as the camera wearer looks down at the sideline gear (frames 1–3) and then turns right toward the court interior (frames 4–5), though it leaves the ground, court boundaries, and background hoop unlabelled. In frames 1 and 3, it detects the person in shorts ahead of the wearer (at roughly 6–8 m in frame 1 and approaching to 4–5 m in frame 3, with their head cropped out of view at the top), and in frames 4 and 5 it tracks the person in the red shirt and blue pants at roughly 3–5 m as the camera pans past them, capturing their full standing contour in frame 4 and their cropped torso and legs at the left edge of frame 5. However, the map is heavily unreliable for object classification and completeness across the scene: in frame 1, the nearer backpack on the ground (at ~1.5 m) is misclassified as a 'baseball glove', while the second bag (~3 m away) and an adjacent sandal are misclassified as 'person' instances. In frame 2, both bags (1.2 m and 2.5 m in front of the wearer) are completely missed and only a single sandal on the left (~3 m away) is misclassified as a 'bird', while in frame 3 the nearer bag at the bottom edge is missed and the second bag (~2.5 m ahead) is again misclassified as a 'person'. Despite these severe class errors and omissions of the jump rope and background structures, the masks still help delineate the sharp spatial boundaries of the motion-blurred person in frame 3 and the standing person in frame 4 against the dark night background.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1–3 and 5, detecting a yellow body skeleton only for the person in the red shirt and blue pants standing on the court to the right in frame 4 at roughly 4–5 m from the camera wearer. In frame 4, the skeleton shows this person standing upright and facing roughly left and slightly toward the camera wearer in three-quarter profile, with their left arm raised so their hand is within direct reach of their own face/head while their right arm hangs down by their hip and their feet rest near the bottom-right of the frame. No magenta hand skeletons are rendered in any frame, and nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer across the sequence. In frame 4, the skeleton clarifies the exact limb articulation and raised-arm posture of the distant person that is somewhat indistinct due to low lighting and motion blur in the RGB image. However, the pose map is highly unreliable whenever bodies are partially out of view or motion-blurred, completely failing to detect the person in shorts at the top of frames 1 and 3 (6–8 m and 4–5 m ahead), the protruding foot at the bottom-right corner of frame 1 (~2 m away), and the cropped torso and legs of the red-shirted person at the left edge of frame 5 (~3–4 m away).
